overview: Host Laura Duggan interviewed Library Director Sam Sednick regarding the history of the Medford Public Library, the development of the new Bloomberg facility, and various community services and specialized collections currently available.

items.title: Introduction of Sam Sednick
items.summary: Host Laura Duggan introduced Sam Sednick, highlighting her background in the Peace Corps and her appointment as Director of the Medford Public Library in April 2026.

items.title: Inspiration and Peace Corps Service
items.summary: Sednick described how her experience building a library for a high school in Lesotho while serving in the Peace Corps inspired her to pursue a career in library science.

items.title: Medford Library History and 150th Anniversary
items.summary: The discussion covered the library's recent 150th anniversary and its historical locations, including the Thatcher Magoon mansion and the former subscription model.

items.title: New Building Planning and Maker Space
items.summary: Sednick detailed her involvement on the building committee and the inclusion of a 'Maker Space' equipped with 3D printers, laser cutters, and sewing machines.

items.title: State Grant Funding and Pandemic Operations
items.summary: Sednick explained the competitive state grant process that funded the new building and reflected on operating out of a temporary space during the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.title: Philanthropy and Naming Rights
items.summary: The director discussed the $3 million donation from Michael Bloomberg in honor of his mother, Charlotte, as well as contributions from Bill Cummings and the Bonsignore family.

items.title: Budget Structure and Friends of the Library
items.summary: Sednick distinguished between city-funded operations and programming funded by the Friends of the Library and the Library Foundation, noting an upcoming book sale in September.

items.title: Volunteer Opportunities and Digital History Project
items.summary: Volunteers assist with book reshelving and a digital local history project that utilizes a Bloomberg grant to make historical newspapers keyword-searchable online.

items.title: Specialized Facilities and 'Library of Things'
items.summary: The facility includes a quiet room for sensory needs and a 'Library of Things' collection that lends unusual items such as kayaks, sledgehammers, and ghost meters.

items.title: Online Databases and Adult Classes
items.summary: The library provides access to resume help, 3D printing badge classes, and digital subscriptions to major newspapers like the New York Times and Boston Globe.

items.title: Youth Services and Therapy Dogs
items.summary: Programming for youth includes age-specific story times and opportunities to read to nonjudgmental therapy dogs to build literacy skills.

items.title: Oral History and Ephemera Collection
items.summary: Assistant Director Jenna Berry leads an oral history project, and the library has begun collecting local election ephemera to preserve modern Medford history.

items.title: Museum Passes and Community Events
items.summary: The Friends of the Library sponsor discounted passes to several local museums, and the library hosts live music events like PorchFest on its patio.

items.title: Local History Room and Artwork
items.summary: Sednick described the preservation of fragile artifacts in the local history room, which currently houses a 24-inch bronze model of the Sarah Bradley Fulton statue.

subject: Medford Public Library History and Services
